pr_title: [Video] Folder stacks, dvd:// paths for movies/episodes, improved playlist selection (recognise episodes on DVDs and Blurays).
pr_body: ## Description I broke something in GIT and it closed #25281. Combination of #24794 and #24997 (now closed). Fixes #16109. Also includes #25140. All merged as they were interlinked and ultimately would all need to work together anyway. There were several issues for folder stacks: - the code to generate folder stacks (`stack://`) was incomplete. - folder stacks were then not recognised at various points in the play pathway (initially, transitioning from one item to another etc..) - playing a stack from the main menu (not movie menu) was also broken (fixed in #24820) - correct length of combined folder stack and streamdetails not saved correctly and not shown in bottom right - routine to determine potential NFO/art path was broken Also fixes: - if you stop a DVD/Bluray on a menu after watching the film the menu length and not the film length is recoded (and shown in bottom right). - one of the regexs for file stacks was to relaxed (see discussion in #24794 comments) - can now handle DVD episodes that are chapters in a single title Adds: - simple menu for DVDs There a few differences now between file and folder stacks. - DVD and Bluray stacks will be built dynamically the first time they are played - and you will be able to move backwards. Once every item is played (and converted to bluray:// or dvd://) then a stack will behave exactly like a file stack. ## Motivation and context Folder stacks are useful for those who have ISOs or DVD/Bluray folders. Selecting episodes from a list of titles was unintuitive and the correct titles were not saved for the future. For example, on The Last of Us (UHD Disc 1) - if I try and play episode 2 (disc 1 contains episodes 1 and 2), I get the following: This demonstrates a number of issues: 1) No clear idea what titles 801 and 851 contain - they actually are both episode 1 (despite us asking to play episode 2) 2) No idea what languages are associated with each title (801 = episode 1 european languages, 851 = episode 1 japanese) Now when I select episode 2 I get the following: This also makes the Videos -> Files -> ... more logical as well. Instead of: ![Before](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/99039295/fbfcd807-71fc-4213-b84f-451e9e8c62fa) We now have: Showing all the episodes on the disc instead of just the first one (with no indication the others are there) and: Allowing you to sellect each episode rather than a random title list. ## How has this been tested? Locally ## What is the effect on users? As above. ## Screenshots (if appropriate): As above. ## Types of change - [ ] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] **Clean up** (non-breaking change which removes non-working, unmaintained functionality) - [X] **Improvement** (non-breaking change which improves existing functionality) - [ ] **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] **Breaking change** (fix or feature that will cause existing functionality to change) - [ ] **Cosmetic change** (non-breaking change that doesn't touch code) - [ ] **Student submission** (PR was done for educational purposes and will be treated as such) - [ ] **None of the above** (please explain below) ## Checklist: - [ ] My code follows the **[Code Guidelines](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/docs/CODE_GUIDELINES.md)** of this project - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation, either Doxygen or wiki - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly - [ ] I have read the **[Contributing](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)** document - [ ] I have added tests to cover my change - [ ] All new and existing tests passed

<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
DVD Folder Stacking is broken.

<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Using the naming convention, such as "d:\movies\Gettysburg (1993) dvd1" and "d:\movies\Gettysburg (1993) dvd2", it will add these to as Videos with no information to the library (they will be listed as "video"), and will not correctly stacked.

## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
DVD Folder Stacking to work correctly.


## Actual Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
DVD Folders labeled dvd1 and dvd2 are added with placeholder metadata, and have to be manually edited, but can never be stacked.


## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

I've looked at the code, and it appears that FileItem.StackFolders correctly identifies patterns, but it appears it does nothing does nothing with the data. 

It also appears that FileItem.StackFiles correctly handles ISO files such as d:\movies\Gettysburg (1993) dvd1.iso and d:\movies\Gettysburg (1993) dvd2.iso.

**What isn't clear** 

- **shoud StackFolders should do something with the stack, or does it expects StackFiles to do something to complete the stacking?**

- Stack Files uses regular expressions that expect a 4 part <title> <Volume> <Ignore period> <Extension>, and it uses the m_videoStackRegExps, not the m_folderStackRegExps that StackFolders uses. When it gets to the regular expression parsing, it looks at the video_ts.ifo file, and splits up the name as VI,  D, EO_TS, IFO, and not "Gettysburg (1993) 2", because it is looking at the file name, not the folder the file is in. 

It appears that if you change file1 and file2 in StackFiles to FilePath1 and FilePath2, that this could fix the problem, but it would likely break ISO stacking.

In looking through the history of this file, it looks like mkortstiege initially made significant changes to this, and would be a good candidate to know/understand what the intent of StackFolders and StackFiles is?

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. in a folder that your library has, make two copies of any dvd folder
2. rename the dvd folder as Movie (2019) dvd1 and another folder as Movie (2019) dvd2
2. start kodi and go to your movies and run update library.

review_comments: Although we are doing it at several places for historical reasons, re-setting item's path after creation is a bug! The path is the identity of an item that must not change during entire lifetime of the instance. We introduced dynpath to keep what actually shall be played.
